newsitem.title: UK: UK's Major says will not rejoin ERM or shadow Euro.
newsitem.headline: UK's Major says will not rejoin ERM or shadow Euro.

text.p: Prime Minister John Major said on Thursday Britain would not rejoin a European exchange rate mechanism and would not shadow the European single currency if the government decided to stay outside the single currency.

"As both...the Chancellor of the Exchequer (Kenneth Clarke) and I have made clear on many occasions, we do not intend to rejoin the so-called ERM Mark Two and we would not wish to institute any policy of shadowing the Euro," he said.
Major was responding to a question from Conservative member of parliament Teddy Taylor, one of a group of ruling party MPs strongly opposed to further European integration.

Major also repeated that the government's commitment to hold a referendum if it decided to join a single European currency during the next parliament meant the plebiscite would be held before the country actually joined the single currency. -- London Newsroom +44 171 542 7768
